annotation.title_clean: Guidance Note on Consumer Protection and the Responsible Adoption and Use of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning by Licensed Financial Institutions in the U.A.E.
annotation.title_en: Guidance Note on Consumer Protection and the Responsible Adoption and Use of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning by Licensed Financial Institutions in the U.A.E.
annotation.summary_en: CBUAE guidance note setting flexible principles for licensed financial institutions' use of AI/ML, focused on consumer protection: governance and board accountability, non-discrimination, transparency and opt-out, data quality and privacy, continuous monitoring, human oversight, and third-party risk. No embodied AI or robotics content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Boards and senior management are accountable for AI/ML systems and outcomes; LFIs should not use AI models they cannot control.
AI must not be discriminatory or manipulative; bias testing annually or upon model change.
Transparency about AI use in high-impact decisions, with disclosures in Arabic and English and consideration of customer opt-out rights.
Privacy-by-design, security-by-design, stress testing and operational resilience.
Continuous monitoring, an AI model inventory, and oversight of third-party AI providers.
